claims.claim: Confirmed as permanent head coach on Friday 22 May 2026, contract until 2028
claims.note: IANS dates the announcement 22 May 2026 and gives the deal to 2028; beIN says contract until 2028.

claims.note: IANS: Amorim sacked in January; Carrick took interim charge.

claims.claim: He was 44 when the deal was announced
claims.note: IANS describes him as 44; consistent with birth date 28 July 1981.

First match in charge a 2-0 win over Manchester City; then 3-2 over Arsenal, then wins over Liverpool, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Tottenham

claims.claim: Premier League Manager of the Month after the Manchester City and Arsenal wins

claims.claim: Called the job 'the ultimate role' in a February 2026 interview with The Football Interview

claims.claim: United won 11 of 16 games under Carrick

claims.claim: Highest Premier League points tally since his arrival
Moved the side from seventh to third and secured Champions League football

claims.claim: Carrick: 'From the moment that I arrived here 20 years ago, I felt the magic of Manchester United'

claims.claim: Move to Tottenham Hotspur in 2004 (causal clause removed)

valueNote: Combines the club's 2026 appointment reporting with a sourced career timeline (transfer, debut, trophies, England caps) and flags where sources disagree (Middlesbrough length, Europa League attribution). No official club or federation source could be opened, so the primary-source gap remains.
summary: All checked claims are confirmed against the opened sources after removing the two unsupported sentences (lower-profile opponents, midfield-performance causal clause). The Middlesbrough length conflict and the Europa League attribution are stated as the sources give them.
